sanskrit: agnim antaś chādayasi puruṣān paśubhiḥ saha | vijāvati prajāvati vi te pāśāṃś cṛtāmasi ||
english: You shelter Agni within, together with men and cattle; O fruitful one, O prolific one — we cut asunder your bonds.

sanskrit: ūrjasvatī ghṛtavatī pṛthivyāṃ nimitā mitā | viśvānnaṃ bibhratī śālā mā hiṃsīḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ ||
english: Rich in vigor, rich in ghee, measured and fixed upon the earth — the hall bearing all food: do not harm the one who receives you.

sanskrit: yas tvā pūrvo nimimāya saṃjabhāra vanaspatīn | prajāyai cakre tvā śāle parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ ||
english: He who first measured you out and gathered together the forest-trees — Parameṣṭhin Prajāpati fashioned you, O hall, for progeny.

sanskrit: namas tasmai namo dātre śālāpataye ca kṛṇmasi | namo 'gnaye pracarate puruṣāya ca te namaḥ ||
english: Homage to him, homage to the giver — and we make obeisance to the lord of the hall; homage to Agni who moves within, and homage to you, O Man.

sanskrit: gobhyo aśvebhyo namo yac chālāyāṃ vijāyate | antarā dyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca yad vyacas tena śālāṃ prati gṛhṇāmi ta imām ||
english: Homage to the cattle and horses that are born in the hall. By the expanse that lies between heaven and earth — by that expanse do I receive this hall of yours.

sanskrit: yad antarikṣaṃ rajaso vimānaṃ tat kṛṇva udaraṃ śevadhibhyaḥ | yac chālāṃ prati gṛṇāmi tasmai ||
english: That which is the intermediate space, the measure of the luminous realm — that I make the womb for treasures; for that for which I praise the hall, be it so.

sanskrit: tṛṇair āvṛtā paladān vasānā rātrīva śālā jagato niveśanī | mitā pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhati hastinīva padvatī ||
english: Covered with grasses, clothed in thatch, like Night the hall is the resting-place of the world; measured, it stands upon the earth, like a great elephant, footed firm.

sanskrit: yā dvipakṣā catuṣpakṣā ṣaṭpakṣā yā nimīyate | aṣṭāpakṣāṃ daśapakṣāṃ śālāṃ mānasya patnīm agnir garbha ivā śaye ||
english: She who is measured with two sides, four sides, six sides — the eight-sided, ten-sided hall, wife of the house-master: Agni lies within her like a child in the womb.

sanskrit: iṭasya te vi cṛtāmy apinaddham aporṇuvan | varuṇena samubjitāṃ mitraḥ prātar vy ubjatu ||
english: I undo what is bound of your wicker-work, uncovering what is covered over; what has been pent up by Varuṇa, may Mitra release it at dawn.

sanskrit: kulāye 'dhi kulāyāṃ kośe kośaḥ samubjitaḥ | tatra marto vi jāyate yasmād viśvaṃ prajāyate ||
english: Nest upon nest, sheath within sheath compressed — therein does the mortal take birth, from whom all the world is born.

sanskrit: catuḥsraktiṃ paricakrāṃ kavibhir nimitāṃ mitām | indrāgnī rakṣataḥ śālām amṛtau somyaṃ sadaḥ ||
english: Four-cornered, furnished with a circuit, measured and built by the sages — Indra and Agni, those two immortal lords of Soma, protect the hall.

sanskrit: mā naḥ pāśān prati muco gurur bhāro laghur bhava | vadhūm iva tvā śāle yatrakāmaṃ bharāmasi ||
english: Do not hurl your bonds back upon us; become light, O heavy burden. Like a bride, O hall, we carry you wherever we wish.

sanskrit: imā āpaḥ pra harāmy ayakṣmā yakṣmanāśanīḥ | gṛhān abhi pra sīdāmy amṛtena sahāgninā ||
english: I carry forward these waters, disease-free, destroyers of disease; I settle into the dwelling together with immortality and with Agni.

sanskrit: pratīcīṃ tvā pratīcīnaḥ śāle praimy ahiṃsatīm | agnir hy antar āpaś ca- -ṛtasya prathamobhā ||
english: Westward I, facing westward, approach you, O hall, unharmful; for Agni within and the waters — both are the foremost of the cosmic order.

sanskrit: svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ prācyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne ||
english: Svāhā to the gods, svāhā to those worthy of svāhā — from the eastern quarter of the hall, homage to its greatness.

sanskrit: svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyo dakṣiṇasyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne ||
english: Svāhā to the gods, svāhā to those worthy of svāhā — from the southern quarter of the hall, homage to its greatness.

sanskrit: svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ pratīcyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne ||
english: Svāhā to the gods, svāhā to those worthy of svāhā — from the western quarter of the hall, homage to its greatness.

sanskrit: svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhya udīcyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne ||
english: Svāhā to the gods, svāhā to those worthy of svāhā — from the northern quarter of the hall, homage to its greatness.

sanskrit: svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyo dhruvāyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne ||
english: Svāhā to the gods, svāhā to those worthy of svāhā — from the fixed (nadir) quarter of the hall, homage to its greatness.

sanskrit: svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhya ūrdhvāyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne ||
english: Svāhā to the gods, svāhā to those worthy of svāhā — from the upper (zenith) quarter of the hall, homage to its greatness.

sanskrit: svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyo diśodiśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne ||
english: Svāhā to the gods, svāhā to those worthy of svāhā — from every quarter of the hall, homage to its greatness.

sanskrit: arātīyor bhrātṛvyasya durhārdo dviṣataḥ śiraḥ | pra vṛścāmīdam ojasā ||
english: The head of the rival, the enemy, the ill-willed adversary who hates us — this I cleave off with might.

sanskrit: varma mahyam ayaṃ maṇiḥ phālāj jātaḥ kariṣyati | tṛpto manthena māgamad rasena saha varcasā ||
english: This amulet, born from the plowshare, shall make armor for me; satisfied with the oblation-drink, may it come with vital sap and with luster.

sanskrit: yat tvā śikvaḥ parāvadhīt takṣā hastena vāsyā | āpas tvā tasmāj jīvalāḥ punantu śucayaḥ śucim ||
english: What the skilled carpenter struck away from you with the adze in his hand — from that may the living waters, pure themselves, purify you, O pure one.

sanskrit: hiraṇyasrag ayaṃ maṇir duhāno vasv akṣitam | śraddhāṃ yajñaṃ maho dadhad gṛhe vasatu no 'tithiḥ ||
english: This amulet, garlanded with gold, milking forth inexhaustible wealth, bearing faith, sacrifice, and greatness — may the guest dwell in our home.

sanskrit: tasmai ghṛtaṃ surāṃ madhv annam annaṃ kṣadāmahe | sa naḥ piteva putrebhyaḥ śreyaḥśreyaś cikitsatu devebhyo maṇir etya ||
english: For him we carve out ghee, surā, honey, and food — let the amulet, having gone to the gods, discern for us ever greater prosperity, as a father does for his sons.

sanskrit: yam abadhnād bṛhaspatir maṇiṃ phālaṃ ghṛtaścutam ugraṃ khadiram ojase | tena tvaṃ dviṣato jahi ||
english: The amulet — the plowshare-piece dripping with ghee, fierce khadira-wood — which Bṛhaspati bound on for might: with that strike down your enemies.

sanskrit: tam agniḥ praty amuñcata- -ājyāya rasāya kaṃ so asmā ājyaṃ duhe | bhūyobhūyaḥ śvaḥśvas tena tvaṃ dviṣato jahi ||
english: Agni fastened it back on — for the sake of clarified butter and vital sap; it milks ghee for him, ever more, day after day. With that strike down your enemies.

sanskrit: yam abadhnād bṛhaspatir maṇiṃ phālaṃ ghṛtaścutam ugraṃ khadiram ojase | tena tvaṃ dviṣato (…) ||
english: The amulet — the plowshare-piece dripping with ghee, fierce khadira-wood — which Bṛhaspati bound on for might: with that [strike down your enemies].

sanskrit: tam indraḥ praty amuñcata- -ojase vīryāya kaṃ so asmai balam id duhe | (…) ||
english: Indra fastened it back on — for might and heroic power; it milks strength alone for him. [With that strike down your enemies.]

sanskrit: taṃ sūryaḥ praty amuñcata tenemā ajayad diśaḥ so asmai varca id duhe | (…) ||
english: Sūrya fastened it back on; with it he conquered these quarters; it milks luster alone for him. [With that strike down your enemies.]
